:::{#exm-huffman-entropy-bound}
#### The bound for the Huffman code of the earlier example

<!-- no-figure: the example is three numbers compared in a sentence -->

The Huffman code of @exm-huffman-code has the codeword lengths $(2, 2, 2, 3, 3)$
for the probabilities $(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)$.
The code below computes its entropy and expected length.

```{r}
#| label: huffman-entropy-bound
p <- c(0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1)
huffman_lengths <- c(2, 2, 2, 3, 3)
entropy <- -sum(p * log2(p))
expected_length <- sum(p * huffman_lengths)
data.frame(entropy, expected_length, upper_bound = entropy + 1)
```

The expected length is $`r round(expected_length, 3)`$ bits.
It lies between the entropy, $`r round(entropy, 3)`$ bits,
and the entropy plus one bit, $`r round(entropy + 1, 3)`$ bits,
as @thm-huffman-entropy-bound says.

:::
